requirements_summary: Quantiva evaluating Redwood for regulated EU workloads. Strong preference for Dedicated (or VPC isolation) in EU region. Must have SIEM-ready audit export (Splunk or S3 preferred; Datadog acceptable) with configurable filtering to reduce noise, plus clear delivery semantics for compliance/IR. They explicitly asked for: (1) stable event_id for dedup, (2) category taxonomy documentation, (3) filter examples (allowlist categories + actor/resource predicates), (4) SLOs/operational visibility (export lag, last success/error), (5) written language for SOC2/ISO questionnaires describing Redwood retention vs customer SIEM retention.
notes:
Account context
- Quantiva is an EU-based risk analytics vendor; internal security team is driving requirements. They’re treating SIEM-ready audit export as a gating control for production approval.

What they care about (quotes/paraphrases)
- “EU residency is non-negotiable. If audit events or model traffic touch US regions, it’s a no.”
- “We need to demonstrate auditability end-to-end: who changed what, when, and evidence that events can be exported to our SIEM reliably.”
- “Filtering is mandatory — we can’t ingest everything; need allowlist by category/action and ability to limit to specific workspaces/projects.”

SIEM export specifics (beta)
- Preferred destinations: S3 (for long-term retention + reprocessing) and Splunk (primary SOC workflow). Datadog is used by app teams but security uses Splunk.
- Delivery guarantees: OK with at-least-once if event_id exists and is stable; asked Redwood to explicitly document expected downstream dedup behavior.
- Backfill: asked for ability to backfill last 7–30 days during initial rollout; also asked what happens if downstream is throttling (do we pause, retry, DLQ?).
- Operational visibility: wants a dashboard view or API response for export health: last successful delivery, lag, error counts per destination.

Filtering requirements (detail)
- Must support category allowlist at minimum (e.g., authn/authz, admin/config changes, key management, model access). They want to exclude high-volume read-only events unless explicitly enabled.
- Wants some resource scoping: only selected workspaces + key admin actions. Also asked if actor can be filtered by type (human vs service account).
- Asked for a full category/action list for documentation + how Redwood will handle new categories (backwards compatibility concerns).

Evidence requests / compliance
- Requested written clarification for SOC2/ISO questionnaires:
  - Redwood’s internal retention of audit logs vs customer responsibility after export
  - Redaction policy / PII minimization (what fields are prohibited)
  - Encryption: in transit and at rest; whether S3 delivery supports SSE-KMS + cross-account role
- They asked if IP address + user agent are included. They will accept inclusion only if documented + justified; otherwise prefer omission/redaction.

Stakeholders / internal ownership
- Redwood: Liam O’Rourke (owner), Colin O’Donnell (SE), Miguel Santos (CSM), Naomi Feldman (PM for beta criteria), Marcus Lin (security semantics).
- Customer: Security lead + platform eng manager (names withheld in CRM per request).

Open questions
- Confirm EU region availability for Dedicated that meets their residency interpretation (including telemetry/ops data boundaries).
- Confirm if they can be included in initial 3–5 beta accounts (and whether their required backfill window fits beta defaults).

Next steps
- Provide category taxonomy + filtering examples (copy/paste snippets OK) + delivery semantics one-pager.
- Offer a security evidence call focused on audit schema v2 + redaction policy + retention vs export responsibilities.
